title: Fabric TCP RST injection sleuth and runbook draft
body:
Summary:

On 2026-04-19 between ~14:03-15:18 UTC we observed intermittent spikes of control-plane reconnections and model-serving stalls for a subset of private deployments in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Symptom set: frequent connection resets (TCP RST) observed on long-lived control-plane and KV-cache connections, increased tail latency for streaming requests, and elevated errors in the connector (GRPC/HTTP2) layer that led to automatic failovers to fallback routing. Impact was partial (12% of customer streams degraded) and resolved via mitigations described below.

Why this doc: not an ops blamestorm — this is a working sleuth log + minimal runbook steps we can vet and fold into the private-deployments runbook. Intended for SREs oncall, infra owners, and customer success if customer-facing notes are needed.

Timeline (abridged):
- 14:03 UTC: Pager fired: control-plane heartbeat misses (alerts from heartbeat-monitoring).
- 14:05 UTC: First oncall ack; initial hypothesis: BGP/peer churn in fabric.
- 14:10 UTC: Packet captures from an affected node (node-7) show bursts of TCP RSTs sourced from 10.200.85.1 (customer-edge firewall IP).
- 14:17 UTC: Cross-checked other affected nodes in same tenant: identical pattern, same source IP for RSTs.
- 14:30 UTC: Short mitigation deployed: increase control-plane connection keepalive probes from 30s -> 10s (to detect/recov faster) and enable conservative reconnect jitter to avoid thundering herd.
- 14:48 UTC: Symptoms reduced but not eliminated; still see RST bursts during high-throughput periods.
- 15:00 UTC: Customer network team engaged (ticket SRE-4321); they confirmed an ASA device with aggressive TCP session-aging policy and inline DPI that will send RST for perceived idle or high-rate flows.
- 15:18 UTC: Longer-term mitigations agreed: (1) add connection pinning and 0-RTT reconnect on client side, (2) advise customer to relax TCP-termination policy or create explicit exception for control-plane ips, (3) add a server-side connection reuse pool to reduce number of distinct TCP flows across the firewall.

Observed evidence:
- tcpdump (node-7) snippet: tcpdump -nn -r sample.pcap -ttt | grep "RST" shows repeated RSTs from 10.200.85.1 -> 10.200.12.7 spaced in short bursts.
- ss output around spike: ss -tanp state established shows many control-plane sockets in ESTABLISHED with low rx/tx but then torn down with RST.
- Application logs: grpc errors with code UNAVAILABLE and immediate CloseNotify in HTTP2 streams. KV cache miss rates spiked (LRU churn) immediately after bursts.
- Packet analysis: sequence numbers indicate RSTs are not in-response to garbage packets (no previous retransmit storm) — appears to be active middlebox injection.

Hypothesis (root cause):
- Active TCP session termination (injection of RST) by an inline firewall/NAT device at customer edge that aggressively ages sessions or treats our long-lived high-throughput multiplexed connections as suspicious. This causes the server (or client) to believe the peer closed the connection; downstream components reclaim KV caches and re-establish new flows, causing cache warm-up and higher latency.

Why this is plausible:
- RST source IP correlates to customer's edge IP reported by their team.
- No BGP flaps or route changes coincident with events (control-plane BGP logs clean).
- RST bursts align with periods of high connection churn and when multiplexing many logical streams over fewer TCP connections.

Immediate mitigations applied (effective):
1) Probe/reconnect tuning (temporary): keepalive -> 10s, TCP_USER_TIMEOUT reduced to allow faster detection/reconnect. This reduced impact window.
2) Application: introduced reconnect jitter and exponential backoff to avoid simultaneous reconnect storms.
3) Ops: temporarily opened a per-customer exception to allow higher idle timeout in the customer's ASA during business hours (agreed in ticket).

Longer-term mitigations and recommendations:
- Server-side connection pooling: implement a connection reuse pool that favors fewer persistent sockets per customer to reduce state tracked by customer firewall. (owner: infra/connection-pool, ETA: 3 sprints)
- Fallback policy: allow safe fallback to alternate region for control-plane heartbeats for affected tenants while preserving data-plane locality. (owner: platform-routing, ETA: 6 weeks)
- Customer guidance: send an engineering note + config snippet for common firewalls (Cisco ASA, Palo Alto, Fortinet) that shows recommended TCP session timeouts and DPI exceptions. (owner: solutions-eng)
- Monitoring: add a short-lived metric: 'tcp_rst_rate_per_customer' and an alert if rate > threshold (owner: observability, ETA: 2 weeks).
- Protocol exploration: evaluate switching certain low-volume heartbeats to QUIC (UDP) to avoid TCP middlebox RST semantics for long-lived, multiplexed control channels. (owner: research/serving-runtime, triage)

Runbook draft excerpt (for oncall page) — minimal steps to triage and mitigate when TCP RST bursts seen:
1) On alert ack, collect immediate artifacts:
   - node tcpdump: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/rst.pcap host <suspected-firewall-ip> or host <node-ip>
   - ss -tanp | grep <control-plane-port> > /tmp/ss.out
   - journalctl -u redwood-controlplane -S "-15m" > /tmp/cp.log
2) Identify RST source: open pcap in tshark or Wireshark: tshark -r /tmp/rst.pcap -Y tcp.flags.rst==1 -T fields -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e tcp.seq -e frame.time_relative | sort | uniq -c
3) Quick mitigation options (ranked):
   A) If source IP is customer-managed and customer ops is reachable: ask them to whitelist our control-plane IPs or increase TCP idle timeout for the flow. (fastest fix)
   B) Increase keepalive frequency / reduce TCP_USER_TIMEOUT for affected node(s) via sysctl for temporary relief.
   C) Enable reconnect jitter on server side (feature flag) to prevent herd reconnections across a tenant.
   D) If the customer permits, route control-plane over alternate egress (if dedicated) to bypass problematic middlebox.
4) If mitigations reduce RSTs: monitor for 30m and close incident. If not: escalate to platform-routing and customer-eng for coordinated deeper network trace.

Post-incident actions (owner assignments):
- infra/connection-pool: draft implementation design and perf impact analysis (owner: Luis Martínez; due 2026-05-10).
- observability: instrument tcp_rst_rate_per_customer + dashboard (owner: Ava Chen; due 2026-04-30).
- solutions-eng: prepare firewall config guidance and email template to customers (owner: Michael O'Connor; due 2026-04-27).
- research: prototype QUIC-based heartbeat for control-plane (owner: Yuki Tanaka; triage in sprint 45).
- SRE oncall handbook: add the runbook excerpt above to private-deployments oncall runbook (owner: Priya Nair; due 2026-04-25).

Open questions & risks:
- If we reduce number of TCP flows (server pooling) we may concentrate failure impact to fewer sockets; what impact does that have when a firewall treats high-throughput single sockets as suspicious? Need to test with lab firewall appliances.
- QUIC exploration has dependency on customer policy — some environments forbid UDP at edge.
- Are there other middleboxes (DPI appliances) that will inject RSTs based on payload heuristics rather than idle time? Need deeper pcap analysis to surface payload-based triggers.

Appendix: useful commands and quick snippets
- capture RSTs: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -nn -s 0 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-rst) != 0 and (host <node-ip> or host <customer-edge-ip>)' -w /tmp/rst.pcap
- show established conns: ss -o state established '( sport = :<control-port> )'
- identify recent resets from conntrack (if using NAT gateway): sudo conntrack -L | grep "ESTABLISHED" | grep <customer-ip>
- quick pcap parse: tshark -r /tmp/rst.pcap -Y tcp.flags.reset==1 -T fields -e frame.time -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e tcp.srcport -e tcp.dstport -e tcp.seq -e tcp.ack

Notes to self (informal):
- Customer said ASA firmware 9.8 had a known aggressive tcp-terminator rule when certain SYN/ACK patterns seen — ask customer for firmware + syslog dump.
- Consider building a small synthetic test harness that opens N long-lived multiplexed connections through a customer's ASA in our lab and measures RST behavior across different rates.

Draft status: please add corrections, additional evidence (pcaps, logs), and any customer communications to linked_artifacts. Once reviewers sign off we'll copy runbook excerpt -> shared runbooks and send solutions-eng config guidance to the customer.

-- Priya
